title: Highest-Paying Allied Health Careers
summary: See the highest-paying allied health careers, overall, as well as those that don't require a degree. See job description, education requirements, & more.
body_markdown:
[Allied health](https://www.stepful.com/post/what-is-allied-health-guide-to-careers) covers more than 200 healthcare professions outside medicine, nursing, and dentistry that support patient care.


The allied health roles we cover here pay between the mid-$40,000s and more than $147,000, and salaries vary widely even among jobs that require the same schooling.


Training time is one factor that can affect pay. The roles at the top of the list below mostly take multiple years of school. Training for the ones at the bottom can be finished in months, if not weeks.


For example, radiation therapists and physical therapists earn a median salary of around $100,000 a year, but radiation therapists typically need an associate degree, while physical therapists need a doctorate. Phlebotomists, who draw blood, earn a median salary of $45,230 but can get trained in a month.


Fortunately, job outlook is one of the most attractive things about careers in allied health. For example, the BLS projects healthcare support jobs will grow[13.3% between 2025 and 2035,](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ecopro.nr0.htm) which is much faster than the average for all occupations at 3.5%.


This guide ranks the 12 highest-paying allied health careers by median salary. We’ll tell you a little about what that job entails, how much education or training it requires, and how in-demand it is. We also rank the highest-paying jobs you can enter without a degree, to get you started in allied health even faster.


## Top 12 Highest-Paying Allied Health Careers


The amount of education and training required for these 12 jobs varies more than you might expect. Six typically require an associate degree, one requires a bachelor’s, three require a master’s, and two require a clinical doctorate.


Every salary in this first list is a median, so it helps to know what that means. The median is the middle wage when you order workers’ earnings from lowest to highest. About half the people in that job earn more and half earn less.


The median gives a better picture of what you can expect to earn than the average because a small number of very high earners can distort the data.


Most of our salary data comes from the[U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)](https://www.bls.gov/) , which tracks wages, employment, and projected job growth across hundreds of occupations. For medical assistants and pharmacy technicians, we use average pay from Stepful’s salary guides, based on recent job postings.


Rank Career Median Salary Typical Education Jobs Job Growth, 2025-2035


1 Medical dosimetrist $147,470 Bachelor’s degree plus accredited dosimetry program 3,500 5% (faster than average)


2 Radiation therapist $105,310 Associate or bachelor’s degree plus certification 17,400 3% (about as fast as average)


3 Physical therapist $102,760 Doctoral or professional degree 283,700 12% (much faster than average)


4 Nuclear medicine technologist $101,370 Associate degree 17,400 4% (about as fast as average)


5 Occupational therapist $100,330 Master’s degree 169,600 15% (much faster than average)


6 Genetic counselor $100,040 Master’s degree 4,200 10% (much faster than average)


7 Dental hygienist $98,100 Associate degree 225,300 8% (much faster than average)


8 Speech-language pathologist $97,870 Master’s degree 193,400 17% (much faster than average)


9 Diagnostic medical sonographer $96,590 Associate degree 92,200 14% (much faster than average)


10 Audiologist $95,780 Doctoral or professional degree 14,200 11% (much faster than average)


11 MRI technologist $95,480 Associate degree; related experience often needed 43,900 8% (much faster than average)


12 Respiratory therapist $82,280 Associate degree 142,000 9% (much faster than average)


### 1) Medical Dosimetrist


Medical dosimetrists help plan radiation treatment for people with cancer and other serious diseases. They calculate the dose and help decide how to deliver it to the right area while limiting damage to healthy tissue.


Most work in hospitals and physicians’ offices, often spending much of the day at a computer.


Medical dosimetrist is the highest-paying allied health role on this list, though there are far fewer jobs compared to most other roles.


- **Median salary:**[$147,470/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/medical-dosimetrists.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 3,500
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 5% (faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Bachelor’s degree and an accredited medical dosimetry program; employers usually require certification

### 2) Radiation Therapist


Radiation therapists run the machines that deliver targeted radiation to people being treated for cancer.


They work mostly in hospitals and outpatient cancer centers, and they often see the same patients five days a week for a month or more.


It is the highest-paying role on this list that typically starts with an associate degree.


- **Median salary:**[$105,310/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/radiation-therapists.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 17,400
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 3% (about as fast as average)
- **Typical education:** Associate degree for entry-level


### 3) Physical Therapist


Physical therapists work in outpatient clinics, hospitals, nursing homes, and patients’ homes. They help people move without pain after an injury, surgery, or stroke.


They need a Doctor of Physical Therapy degree, which[typically lasts three years](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/physical-therapists.htm) after they get their bachelor’s degree, plus a state license.


- **Median salary:**[$102,760/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/physical-therapists.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 283,700
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 12% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Doctor of Physical Therapy degree, plus a state license


### 4) Nuclear Medicine Technologist


Like radiation therapy, this job pays six figures and typically starts with an associate degree from an accredited program.


Nuclear medicine technologists give patients small doses of radioactive drugs, then use scanners to track how those drugs move through the body. Most work in hospitals, with the rest in imaging clinics, physician offices, and diagnostic labs.


- **Median salary:**[$101,370/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/nuclear-medicine-technologists.htm) **‍**
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 17,400 **‍**
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 4% (about as fast as average) **‍**
- **Typical education:** Associate degree


### 5) Occupational Therapist


Occupational therapists help patients relearn the everyday skills an injury or illness took away, whether that means getting dressed alone or returning to work.


They work in hospitals, schools, outpatient clinics, and homes.


This job will remain in high demand over the next decade.


- **Median salary:**[$100,330/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/occupational-therapists.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 169,600
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 15% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Master’s degree


### 6) Genetic Counselor


Genetic counselors help people understand their risk of inherited conditions. They review genetic test results with patients and families and help them decide how to respond.


Only 4,200 people hold this job nationwide, so it is a small field with relatively few openings.


- **Median salary:**[$100,040/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/genetic-counselors.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 4,200
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 10% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Master’s degree


### 7) Dental Hygienist


Dental hygienists work in dentists’ offices cleaning teeth, screening patients for oral disease, and teaching people how to take care of their mouths at home.


Every state licenses hygienists, and licensing usually requires an accredited program plus written and clinical exams.


- **Median salary:**[$98,100/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/dental-hygienists.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 225,300
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 8% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Associate degree


### 8) Speech-Language Pathologist


Speech-language pathologists treat problems with speech, language, and swallowing in patients of every age.


Schools employ a large share of them, and the rest work in hospitals, private practices, and nursing facilities.


At 17% projected growth, this field is growing faster than anything else on the list.


- **Median salary:**[$97,870/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/speech-language-pathologists.htm)
- **Number of jobs in U.S.:** 193,400
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 17% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Master’s degree


### 9) Diagnostic Medical Sonographer


Sonographers mostly work in hospitals but also work in outpatient imaging centers. They use ultrasound machines to create the images doctors need to evaluate or diagnose conditions.


We mostly think of these as pregnancy scans, but hearts, blood vessels, and abdominal organs all get imaged this way as well.


- **Median salary:**[$96,590/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/diagnostic-medical-sonographers.htm)
- **Number of jobs in U.S.:** 92,200
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 14% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Associate degree


### 10) Audiologist


Audiologists diagnose and treat hearing and balance problems, which includes fitting hearing aids and helping patients communicate.


They work in audiology clinics, physician offices, hospitals, and schools. The job requires a Doctor of


Audiology degree, which[typically takes four years](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/audiologists.htm) after a bachelor’s degree, plus a license in every state.


- **Median salary:**[$95,780/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/audiologists.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 14,200
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 11% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Doctor of Audiology degree, plus a state license


### 11) MRI Technologist


MRI technologists position patients and operate scanners that use magnetic fields to create detailed images of the body.


They work mostly in hospitals and imaging centers.


An associate degree is the typical education requirement, and many enter the field after working in radiologic technology.


- **Median salary:**[$95,480/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/radiologic-technologists.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 43,900
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 8% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Associate degree, often with related work experience; employers typically require or prefer certification


### 12) Respiratory Therapist


Respiratory therapists make less money than the rest of this list, but an associate degree is the typical education requirement.


They treat people who are struggling to breathe, including premature infants and adults living with COPD. Most work in[hospitals](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/respiratory-therapists.htm) , often on nights and weekends.


- **Median salary:**[$82,280/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/respiratory-therapists.htm) **‍**
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 142,000 **‍**
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 9% (much faster than average) **‍**
- **Typical education:** Associate degree

## Highest-Paying Allied Health Careers That Don’t Require a Degree


Many allied health careers pay competitively without requiring an associate or bachelor’s degree. Many of these roles require a postsecondary nondegree award. That usually means completing a certificate or diploma program after high school, which may prepare you for certification or licensing. Some roles offer on-the-job training instead. Requirements vary by state and employer.


Although pay is lower than the list above, the job outlook for these roles is strong, though benefits, schedules, and job availability vary by employer and location.

8 Phlebotomy technician $45,230 Postsecondary nondegree award 143,900 7% (much faster than average)

*Pay is median unless marked as an average. Medical assistant and pharmacy technician averages come from Stepful’s salary guides, updated Sept. 26, 2026. The other figures are BLS medians for May 2025. The list is ordered by the figures shown, but the sources and measures differ.*


### 1) Hearing Aid Specialist


Hearing aid specialists test hearing to help select, fit, and adjust hearing aids. They also show people how to use and care for the devices.


This role has a shorter training path than audiology and the highest median pay on our no-degree list. Check your state’s licensing and training requirements before choosing a program.


- **Median salary:**[$65,160/year](https://www.bls.gov/emp/tables/occupational-projections-and-characteristics.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 11,200
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 19% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** High school diploma or GED plus on-the-job training; state requirements vary


[Take the Quiz!](https://www.stepful.com/healthcare-career-quiz)


### 2) Surgical Technologist


[Surgical technologists](https://www.stepful.com/post/what-surgical-techs-do-duties-responsibilities) set up the operating room, sterilize the instruments, and pass tools to the surgeon during an operation.


Most[surgical techs](https://www.stepful.com/post/where-do-surgical-techs-work) —often called[scrub techs](https://www.stepful.com/post/what-is-a-scrub-tech) —work in hospitals, while others work in outpatient centers and physicians’ offices.


- **Median salary:**[$64,650/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/surgical-technologists.htm#tab-5) **‍**
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:**[118,400](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/surgical-technologists.htm#tab-6) **‍**
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 5% (faster than average) **‍**
- **Typical education:** Postsecondary nondegree award


[Learn about Stepful's 4-Month Online Surgical Tech Program](https://www.stepful.com/surgical-tech)[Learn more](https://www.stepful.com/surgical-tech)


### 3) Paramedic


Paramedics handle emergency calls and provide advanced care before a patient reaches the hospital, including IV medications and cardiac monitoring.


Training goes well beyond the EMT level, and the pay reflects it. Paramedics make about[$16,000 more a year than EMTs](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/emts-and-paramedics.htm) .


- **Median salary:**[$60,600/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/emts-and-paramedics.htm) **‍**
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:**[102,200](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/emts-and-paramedics.htm#tab-6) **‍**
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 6% (faster than average) **‍**
- **Typical education:** Postsecondary nondegree award or associate degree, plus state licensure and supervised field experience


### 4) Massage Therapist


Massage therapists work the body’s soft tissue to relieve pain, treat injuries, and help clients relax. They work in spas, chiropractic and physical therapy offices, hotels, and clients’ homes.


Most states require a license, and[part-time schedules are common](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/massage-therapists.htm) , so actual annual earnings may be lower than the full-time equivalent shown here.


- **Median salary:**[$58,450/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/massage-therapists.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 155,400
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 15% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Postsecondary nondegree award


### 5) Medical Records Specialist


Medical records specialists organize patient health information and check it for accuracy. Some assign the medical codes used for billing and insurance reimbursement.


They work in hospitals, physicians’ offices, and other healthcare settings, usually with little direct patient contact.


- **Median salary:**[$51,140/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/medical-records-and-health-information-technicians.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 200,700
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 8% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Postsecondary certificate is typical; some qualify with a high school diploma, while employers may prefer certification


### 6) Dental Assistant


[Dental assistants](https://www.stepful.com/post/what-is-a-dental-assistant-what-do-they-do) prepare patients and instruments, hand tools to the dentist during procedures, take X-rays where state rules allow it, and handle sterilization. Almost all work in dentists’ offices, and most work full-time.


[Each state has its own requirements](https://www.stepful.com/post/dental-assistant-requirements-by-state) for training, certification, and licensing. Stepful’s[Certified Dental Assistant](https://www.stepful.com/dental-assistant) program takes four months to complete and prepares students for the Dental Assisting National Board's Radiation Health and Safety (RHS) exam.


- **Median salary:**[$48,070/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/dental-assistants.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 388,600
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 7% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Postsecondary nondegree award


[Learn about Stepful's Online Dental Assistant Program](https://www.stepful.com/dental-assistant)


[Explore Program](https://www.stepful.com/dental-assistant)


### 7) Optician


Opticians help people choose eyeglasses and contact lenses, fit frames, and repair eyewear. Most work in optometrists’ offices or retail stores.


You can often learn on the job, though some states require a license and specific training or supervised experience.


- **Median salary:**[$47,260/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/opticians-dispensing.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 74,300
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 4% (about as fast as average)
- **Typical education:** High school diploma or GED plus on-the-job training; state licensing requirements vary


### 8) Phlebotomy Technician


[Phlebotomists](https://www.stepful.com/post/what-is-a-phlebotomist-and-what-do-they-do) draw blood for testing, transfusions, research, and donation. It's a skill you can learn quickly, and it can get you into a hospital, doctor’s office, or lab environment fast.


This is one of the easiest[entry-level healthcare jobs](https://www.stepful.com/post/entry-level-healthcare-jobs) to get into. Some programs take only a few weeks, while others take longer.


Coursework may be online, but programs typically include hands-on clinical training. Compare total cost, length, and certification requirements before enrolling.


- **Median salary:**[$45,230/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/phlebotomists.htm)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 143,900
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 7% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Postsecondary nondegree award


### 9) EMT


Emergency Medical Technicians (EMTs) respond to 911 calls and assess patients. They provide basic life support and transport people to the hospital.


All states require EMTs to be licensed. Exam and skills requirements vary by state, and most states use[National Registry](https://www.nremt.org/EMT/Certification) certification.


- **Median salary:**[$44,470/year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/emts-and-paramedics.htm) **‍**
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:**[181,900](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/healthcare/emts-and-paramedics.htm#tab-6) **‍**
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 6% (faster than average) **‍**
- **Typical education:** Postsecondary nondegree award


### 10) Medical Assistant


[Medical assistants](https://www.stepful.com/post/what-is-a-medical-assistant) (MAs) do both clinical and administrative tasks. They can take a patient’s vital signs and prep them for an exam or schedule an appointment and update medical records.


They[work mostly in](https://www.stepful.com/post/where-do-medical-assistants-work) physicians' offices, outpatient clinics, and hospitals.


Stepful’s online[Certified Medical Assistant Program](https://www.stepful.com/medical-assistant) takes five months to complete and includes two live, 90-minute classes per week. The program prepares students to earn the NHA’s[Certified Clinical Medical Assistant (CCMA) credential](https://www.stepful.com/post/certified-clinical-medical-assistant) .


- **Average salary:**[$44,312/year](https://www.stepful.com/medical-assistant-salaries/united-states)
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 833,900
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 13% (much faster than average)
- **Typical education:** Postsecondary nondegree award

### 11) Pharmacy Technician


[Pharmacy technicians help](https://www.stepful.com/post/what-is-a-pharmacy-technician) pharmacists fill prescriptions, track inventory, and handle most of the counter and phone work in a pharmacy. They[mostly work in](https://www.stepful.com/post/where-can-pharmacy-technicians-work) retail pharmacies and hospitals.


Some training programs[take about four months](https://www.stepful.com/post/how-long-it-takes-to-become-a-pharmacy-technician-length-of-school-training) , and you may need to be[licensed in some states](https://www.stepful.com/post/pharmacy-technician-license-requirements-by-state) .


Stepful’s[Online Pharmacy Technician Program](https://www.stepful.com/pharmacy-tech) prepares you for national certification and is ASHP/ACPE-accredited in some states. The academic work is 100% online and includes support for finding in-person clinical hours.


- **Average salary:**[$44,056/year](https://www.stepful.com/pharmacy-technician-salaries/united-states) **‍**
- **Number of jobs in the U.S.:** 471,200 **‍**
- **Job growth rate, 2025-2035:** 6% (faster than average) **‍**
- **Typical education:** High school diploma or GED

## Highest-Paying Allied Health Careers FAQs


### What is the highest-paying allied health career?


Medical dosimetry, at a median salary of $147,470 a year, is No. 1 among the careers covered here. Radiation therapy, at $105,310, is the highest-paying role on this list that typically starts with an associate degree.


### Can you make good money in allied health without a four-year degree?


Yes. Hearing aid specialists earn a median salary of $65,160, surgical technologists $64,650, and paramedics $60,600, and all offer entry paths without a four-year degree. Six of the 12 careers in our first list typically start with an associate degree, though some also require related experience, certification, or licensing.


### Do allied health salaries vary by state?


Quite a bit, so check your own area to find out what a role pays where you live. Stepful’s medical assistant and pharmacy technician salary guides include state and city figures, and BLS publishes wage estimates by location. Pay also depends on your work environment, experience, and employer.


### What allied health careers pay well and don’t require years of school?


Hearing aid specialist ($65,160), surgical technologist ($64,650), paramedic ($60,600), and massage therapist ($58,450) are among the higher-paying roles with entry paths that do not require a college degree. Training time varies. Dental assisting, pharmacy tech, medical assisting, and phlebotomy have annual pay figures of about $44,000 to $48,000, and many programs take a year or less. If you're looking for help paying for school, check out our[guide to allied health scholarships](https://www.stepful.com/post/allied-health-scholarships) .


### Which allied health jobs are growing the fastest?


Among the careers covered here, hearing aid specialists lead with 19% projected growth from 2025 to 2035. Speech-language pathology follows at 17%, occupational therapy and massage therapy at 15%, diagnostic sonography at 14%, and medical assisting at 13%. For comparison, BLS projects 3.5% growth across all U.S. jobs.


### Do these jobs require a license or certification?


Many do, and the rules vary by role and state. Dental hygienists, physical therapists, and audiologists are licensed in every state. Most states license massage therapists, and dental assistant requirements range from on-the-job training to an accredited program plus an exam. Check your state’s requirements before enrolling in training.
